title: The derby mute and the kettle mute
summary: He made a derby mute holder from a coat hanger, got a derby by mail, gave one up to a visiting musician, and made a kettle-pot mute for Nelson.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Did you hold it or have it on a rack?

I took a hanger, a clothes hanger, and I made a hook. I used to put it on the stand like you did stand. Like a music stand. Yeah, like that. So after that, well later on, after that, Harrison was born, he gave me one of them, what you call it? Yeah, the regular rack. The regular rack. But I made it myself, you see? And I tell you, what happened? I sent off, that man that wore a line sent off for the same for me. So he, most of the first used them other kind of derby, but they had it guilted. Yeah. With that guilt. Oh yeah. I got it in that derby yet. That's the same derby yet. I got that same derby yet. So alright. So when I, when I sent off and got that derby, a white fella came from Chicago or New York, somewhere he came from. And the derby just had, it just had came in, you see? And he seen it. Well he's a musician. He wanted it. You know? He wanted that derby. So, I told the man, I know it, it was my derby, you see? I told the man, let the man have it. You see? I let the man have the derby, you see? And the man sent off and got another one for me. Oh yeah. Man, it's the first time he had seen one himself. You see? So I was the only one that had one of them derby. Most of them had another kind of derby, but guilted. Yeah. You see?

That's right. That's what they had, you see? So, and everybody seen with that thing, man, say, why ain't the derby got that pot from, it's called a pot, you know what I mean? Yeah. I said, where you got that thing from? I said, man, I sent off and got that.
Well that thing you made, you made that, that is a little pot, the pan that, uh, Yeah, I made that out of the kettle.
That Murray Nelson uses. I made that out of the kettle. A little kettle pot, you know? Yeah.
Teakill, you know what I mean?

Yeah. I cut the top off, you see? Yeah. And sometimes, you know how I mean, sometimes you be sitting down, you know what I mean, you think about things, you know? Yeah. And you know what I mean, you come to, you know what I mean, I said, I'm going make a, I said, I'm going to make a, what you call it, a derby for, for Nelson, you know what I mean? And I had that kettle there, I said, I'm going to take this kettle, you know, and I'm going to cut it. Really? I said, that makes a nice, what you call it, you know what I mean?
I tried. Sounds wonderful, it works good with the handle.
Yeah, and then I tried it on with my horn, you know what I mean? I said, that's going to sound good, you know what I mean? Yeah. So, well, what else you got there?
